item.title: Research Interventionalist
item.description: The Research Interventionalist is a member of the Center for Research and Scholarly Development (CRDS) in the School of Nursing at Vanderbilt University and is a skilled scientific professional responsible for direct outreach, bilingual communication and administrative support, offering hands on experience in participant recruitment and community engaged research. This community-based study focuses on Korean-based recruitment. This is a part-time, flex position that is fully remote. | Key Functions and Expected Performance: Running stellar population synthesis code, analyzing output, plotting and presenting results, weekly meetings to discuss progress, writing up results. Qualifications Ability to run stellar population synthesis codes, analyze scientific data Preferred Qualifications Good communication skills. Supervisory Relationships: This position does not have supervisory responsibility; this position reports administratively to the faculty PI & functionally to the Administrative Manager. Education and Certifications: • A Masters Degree from an accredited institution of higher education is preferred. Experience and Skills: 1 year of experience with long gamma-ray burst population modeling | Key Functions and Expected Performance: Dealing with cosmological simulation data, running large-scale structure codes, analyzing output, plotting and presenting results, weekly meetings to discuss progress, writing up results. Qualifications Ability to work with large simulations, analyze scientific data Preferred Qualifications Good communication skills. Supervisory Relationships: This position does not have supervisory responsibility; this position reports administratively to the faculty PI & functionally to the Administrative Manager. Education and Certifications: • A Masters Degree from an accredited institution of higher education is preferred. Experience and Skills: 1 year of experience with modeling primordial black holes in cosmological simulations | The Spatial Patterns and Access to Care for Engagement and HIV Suppression (SPACES) study seeks a part-time, Spanish-fluent Research Assistant.
